instrument: scripts/mutation-probe.mjs (with --strict in gateArgs), an instrumented reachability run that writes a stderr marker on every entry into the catch block, and a 23-construction filesystem battery comparing existsSync with statSync and realpathSync
probeMissions: norules — `runward init --example` copied to <tmp>/pm/norules/proj with `runward/rules/` DELETED, so the mission carries no local rule corpus and `circularEvidence` calls `realpathOr` on a path that does not exist. A project-level `rules/x.md` was added and cited as `file:rules/x.md` so that an absolute resolved path is compared against the missing-directory prefix. Baseline on a pristine tree: exit 0, verdict clean, 0 gaps. This is the mission built specifically to ENTER the catch.
self-gate — runward's own mission, `check --strict --json` with no `--path`. Baseline: exit 0. runward's own repository also has no `runward/rules/` directory, so the catch is live here too.

esc — a project with no repository marker above it, whose `hexa-architecture` row cites eight pointers covering every refusal branch: a symlink to /etc, an absolute path, a `..` escape, a directory, a FIFO, a mode-000 file, a file inside a mode-111 directory and a symlink that stays inside the project. Baseline: exit 1, 7 conformance gaps. Exercises `realpathOr` on the three evidence bases and on every resolved pointer.

ws2, d24, d25, shallow — the four workspace/containment missions described in repoRootAbove.json, used in the reachability run to check whether the catch is entered when the enclosing-repository fallback and the root walk are exercised.

Reachability run — the catch block was instrumented to write `REALPATHOR-CATCH <code> <path>` to stderr without changing its return value, and `check --strict --json` was run on all six built missions, on runward's own mission, and once with `--freeze` (the seal writer, the other consumer of this helper).

verdicts.evidence: COULD NOT CLEAR at the call sites that carry the risk — filed as a hole on that ground, and the ground is measured. Ran `node scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function realpathOr` on norules, on the self-gate and on esc: `no observable difference` in all three, exit code and full JSON payload byte-identical (ledgers reports/mutation/probe-realpathOr-{norules,selfgate,esc}.jsonl). The instrumented reachability run then showed WHY, and it is not because the catch is dead: it is entered 41 times on norules and 46 times on runward's OWN mission, every single time with `ENOENT` and every single time for the same argument, `<mission>/runward/rules` — the `rulesHome` call in circularEvidence, on a mission that keeps no local rule corpus. On ws2, d24, d25, esc, shallow and the `--freeze` seal path it is entered ZERO times. So exactly one of the six call sites is reachable by any mission I could build, and at that site the mutant is inert: `rulesHome` is used only in `abs === rulesHome` and `abs.startsWith(rulesHome + sep)`, `abs` is always an absolute realpath, and `undefined` makes the first false and turns the second into `startsWith("undefined/")`, which no absolute path satisfies — the same two false answers the pristine value (a path to a directory that does not exist) produces. That is measured as identical on the two missions where the catch fires 41 and 46 times. The other five call sites — the three evidence bases at L317, the pointer's own realpath at L325, the marker directory at L347, the manifest at L380, the seal keys at L669/678 — are all handed a path that has just been proven to exist, and a 23-construction filesystem battery (plain file, directory, FIFO, character devices, socket, broken symlink, symlink cycle, 45-link chain, self-referential directory symlink at 8/31/40 hops, directory-symlink chains at 31 and 39, mode-000 and mode-111 directories, mode-000 file, 255-character component, 1200-character resolved path, NUL byte) found ZERO paths on Node v24.18.0 / macOS for which `existsSync` is true and `realpathSync` throws — the battery in fact found the opposite asymmetry (a 40-hop self-referential symlink where `existsSync` fails with ELOOP and `realpathSync` succeeds), so realpathSync is the more permissive of the two and cannot be made to throw where existsSync accepted. What remains is exactly what the function's own contract is written for: `The real path, or the input when it cannot be resolved (a broken link, a race)`. The broken-link half is the rulesHome case, and it is inert. The race half is at L325, and there the mutant does not degrade a message — it makes `real` undefined, and the very next statement is `real.startsWith(baseAbs + sep)`, a TypeError, which is the `an unreadable file was a crash rather than a verdict, and --json stopped being JSON` class already recorded as RWD-2026-0019. Nothing in the suite, the self-gate or any mission I could build reddens if the fail-safe return stops holding. I refused to base a verdict on a deliberately raced tree, since ADR-0046's amendment of 2026-08-20 forbids a verdict that depends on the state of the machine. Work this creates: a test that forces `realpathSync` to fail on a path the caller has already accepted and pins that the resolver still answers a path rather than throwing.
